narrative: Status-neutral HIV prevention and care approach (Amendment 2024, section 4.1). Everyone starts with an HIV test. A negative result leads to the prevention pathway, which prevents getting HIV: people are offered powerful prevention tools such as PrEP, condoms, harm reduction (for example syringe services programmes) and supportive services to stay HIV negative; components are high-impact HIV prevention and HIV and STD testing. A positive result leads to the treatment pathway, which prevents transmitting HIV: people enter primary care and are offered effective treatment and supportive services to achieve and maintain viral suppression; components are effective treatment and HIV primary care. A person on the prevention pathway who is newly diagnosed with HIV moves to the treatment pathway. Both pathways share culturally inclusive and responsive quality care, and prevention and treatment of syndemic infections.

* If child is >6/52: Continue or restart NVP until the mother is undetectable
